description: The local bug-report store (PianoidCore/logs/reports; the same store as the bug button, the automatic reports and the assistant's bug_report tool): list the reports with their triage state and update a report's status (dev-obuf1). Filing a new report is the assistant's bug_report tool, not a registry command. A stored report can be sent to the team's GitHub repo as an issue (bug.file_github / bug.sync_github, dev-bugsync) so the developers' agents pick it up and fix it; bug.github_preview shows the exact issue first.

commands.name: bug.list
commands.title: List the bug reports
commands.description: Report summaries newest first: reportId, source (assistant / auto / manual), kind (app_bug / environment / feature_request, or the fault kind of an automatic report), title, component, severity, status (open / fixed / wontfix / duplicate) and the resolution (note, commits). Read it before filing a report so you do not re-file one that is already open or fixed; a fixed one names the commit that fixed it.

kind.description: app_bug, environment, feature_request, or an automatic fault kind

commands.name: bug.set_status
commands.title: Update a bug report's status
commands.description: Set a report's status (open / fixed / wontfix / duplicate), severity or kind (e.g. re-class to feature_request). A non-open status needs a resolution note; duplicate also needs duplicate_of; give the commit(s) of a fix (e.g. "Core d99e5a0"). Only when the user asks or confirms, e.g. after verifying a fix with a read or a render.

report_id.description: the reportId or a unique prefix of at least 6 characters

resolution.description: what fixed it / why not / of what it is a duplicate

commands.name: bug.github_config
commands.title: GitHub sync settings of this machine
commands.description: Whether this machine can send bug reports to GitHub: the target repo, configured (a token is set; the token itself is never shown), where the token comes from, auto_send (off / manual / all) and the machine label. Not configured: the message says what the user must set (an operation for the user, never for you).

commands.name: bug.github_preview
commands.title: Preview a report's GitHub issue
commands.description: Dry run: the exact GitHub issue (title, labels, body) that bug.file_github would post for one report, and whether it would create a new issue or update the existing one. Writes nothing; works without a token. Show it to the user before sending.

report_id.description: the reportId or a unique prefix of at least 6 characters

commands.name: bug.file_github
commands.title: Send a bug report to GitHub
commands.description: Send one stored report to the team's GitHub repo as an issue (sends data outside this machine: title, description, build SHAs, preset, layout, action history, a trimmed config snapshot; secrets and emails are redacted). Idempotent: a report already filed updates its issue (status both ways: a closed issue marks the report fixed; a report marked fixed here closes the issue) instead of filing a duplicate. Returns the issue number and url. Only when the user asks or agrees; file the report first (bug_report) when it is not in the store.

report_id.description: the reportId or a unique prefix of at least 6 characters

dry_run.description: build the issue only (prefer bug.github_preview: it needs no confirm)

commands.name: bug.sync_github
commands.title: Sync the bug reports with GitHub
commands.description: Refresh every report already sent to GitHub (status both ways, the text when it changed) and send up to limit unsent reports matching the filter (default: open manual + assistant reports, oldest first). Automatic fault reports are sent only with source auto or all. Run it with dry_run first to list what would be sent.

source.description: assistant, manual, auto, all, or a comma list; default manual,assistant

since.description: ISO time: only reports created at or after it
